analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Rotation into hyperscalers and out of semis; Starlink aspirations; NEM mixed; BT beat; Swisscom OFCF raise; DT mixed; JCD beats
key_insights: Tech saw a sharp rotation into hyperscalers and out of semis and datacentre infrastructure. Investors read the Democratic midterm win as making new datacentre builds harder and existing power-secured compute more valuable.
QQQ finished up 1% after gaining as much as 2.5% early. SPY rose 1.6% and VIX fell 2-3 points. Semis fell 3%, after dropping as much as 5% intraday, underperforming QQQ by 4 percentage points.
The US desk's largest thematic flow was buying hyperscalers versus selling semis, from both long-only and hedge fund clients. Europe showed one-way long-only supply across AI names (ASML, IFX, ENR).

AMZN rose 7-8%, MSFT 4-7%, GOOGL 5-6% and META 3%, with Apple also strong. Combined Mag7-style market-value gains approached $750bn-$1tn. CoreWeave fell 7-11% and Nebius 4-6%. MU and some semis were weaker while NVDA was only slightly lower.

Main debate: whether a Democratic win slows the US AI datacentre buildout through tighter permitting, water and power rules, fewer tax breaks and temporary moratoria. Brad Gerstner argued regulatory friction could stop 10-15 GW of expected 2027 capacity.

GIR sees only 20GW in the US, well below the Street, and sees more risk in 2028. SemiAnalysis says 16.7GW of planned 2028 Texas capacity is at risk. Street forecasts are well above 30GW, so the election adds political risk on top of bullish estimates.

Counterview: most 2027 capacity is already under construction or permitted, Texas moratoria would be constrained by the legislature, and many local bans hit areas with little activity. A broad shutdown is unlikely and delays and higher costs are the real risk. GIR expects datacentre focus to fade after the midterms.

If short-term delays occur, installed power-secured compute becomes more valuable. Hyperscalers AMZN and MSFT are seen as near-term winners while pure new-build names (ORCL expansions, NEOS, SPCX, pure-play AI cloud) lag.

Semis sceptics raise a risk that the semis narrative flips to an inventory correction if power and sites lag chip deliveries. The FT reported AWS takes delivery of about $3bn of Nvidia GB300 racks per month and stages some in warehouses because certain sites lack power. Microsoft made a similar comment in Nov 2025.
Second debate: sustained AI growth requires the cost of compute to keep falling, and higher compute costs reduce displacement pressure on traditional software and media.

SpaceX signed a deal with Qualcomm for Dragonwing Cellular Infrastructure platforms to support Starlink Mobile terrestrial base stations. US nationwide rollout is planned to begin in 2027 with tens of thousands of sites. US telcos ignored the news. The desk sees it as negative for Ericsson and to a lesser extent Nokia.
NEM mixed: organic growth 12.5% vs street 13.6%, Design 6.5% vs street 8.5%, Build 23.6% vs street 22%. EBITDA 1% ahead, FCF conversion above 100%, group guidance reiterated.

DT mixed: revenue, EBITDA AL and OFCF beat and FY guidance raised marginally for the US. Buyback of EUR2bn vs Street EUR3bn disappointed, and Handelsblatt reports DT still pursues a merger with T-Mobile US.

BT beat on service revenue, EBITDA (3% ahead) and line loss, but OFCF missed on higher capex. FY guidance reiterated excluding TalkTalk. Triennial pension deficit is GBP2.7bn, to be substantially replaced with zero-coupon bonds.
Swisscom: revenue beat by 1.4%, reported EBITDAaL missed by 1.2% but beat excluding E39m restructuring. OFCF guidance raised to above CHF2.0bn from around CHF2.0bn.

SES Q3 beat with adjusted EBITDA 12.6% ahead, FY capex guidance cut to about EUR600mn from EUR700mn, and the CMD delayed to March. Bouygues beat with Equans COPA margin guidance raised to at least 5.5%. JCD Q3 organic growth +6.6% vs ~5% guidance, Q4 guided to about 6%.

US overnight: QCOM fell 7.5% after hours on weak margin and earnings guidance with GIR cutting estimates 8%. ARM fell 1.7% after hours on a royalty miss. COHR rose 7.6% on a better guide. HUBS guided Q4 growth to 12% vs 14.5-15% expected. APP rose 20% on a revenue beat, strong guide and $3.2bn buyback. SNAP reported mixed Q3 with ad growth slowing to low-to-mid single digits.

earnings_insights: NEM: reported revenue in line, organic growth 12.5% vs street 13.6%, Design 6.5% vs street 8.5%, Build 23.6% vs street 22%. EBITDA 1% ahead, FCF conversion above 100%, group guidance reiterated, Manage and Media outlooks lowered.
SINCH: topline, organic gross profit growth (c.4% yoy ex-fx) and EBITDA broadly in line. FCF EUR967mn reported, significantly above consensus.
NEXI: revenues +1.4% reported vs street 1.5%, Merchant Services +1.7%, EBITDA 2% ahead, guidance reiterated.

DT: revenue, EBITDA AL and OFCF beat, FY guidance raised marginally for the US. Germany EBITDA growth +1.5% YoY in 3Q26 and needs at least +3.5% in 4Q26 vs consensus just over 4%. Buyback EUR2bn vs Street EUR3bn. Guidance c.EUR11bn vs consensus EUR10.98bn.
BT: service revenue 0.6% ahead, EBITDA 3% ahead, line loss better, OFCF missed on higher capex. Openreach line loss 175k vs street 197k. FY guidance reiterated, excluding TalkTalk.
Swisscom: revenue 1.4% ahead, reported EBITDAaL 1.2% below, a beat excluding E39m restructuring. OFCF guidance now above CHF2.0bn vs around CHF2.0bn prior.
SES: Q3 revenue 1.3% ahead of consensus, adjusted EBITDA 12.6% ahead. FY capex guided to around EUR600mn vs EUR700mn previously and consensus EUR706mn.
Bouygues: about 1% revenue beat and 2% COPA beat. Equans COPA margin guidance raised from 5.2% to at least 5.5%, group guidance raised to slight growth.
JCD: 3Q26 organic revenue growth +6.6% vs company guidance of about 5%. Digital Out-of-Home +15.3%, programmatic +37.5%. 4Q guided to about 6% organic growth.
AUTO LN: H1 revenue below expectations on weaker vehicle and accessory sales, EBIT better, FY27 guidance reiterated.

QCOM (reported 11/4 after close): in-line quarter, revenue meeting expectations, better December-quarter revenue guidance, weaker earnings and margin guidance. Smartphone market now expected to decline low-to-mid teens in CY26 and be flat to down slightly in CY27.
ARM (reported after close): revenue and EPS guidance above Street, royalty revenue missed again, licensing strong with four new CSS customers. Targets $2bn AGI CPU revenue in FY27-28.
COHR: in line on the quarter, gross margin missed by about 10-30bps, better guide. FY27 pro forma growth above 60%, above $11.2B vs Street $10.63B on a roughly $7.0B FY26 base.
HUBS: Q3 revenue +17% in constant currency vs 15.5-16% expected. Q4 growth guide 12% vs 14.5-15% expected. FY net revenue retention to fall about 2 pp and Q4 net customer additions below 5,000.
APP: biggest revenue beat since Q4 2025, guidance well above expectations, $3.2bn buyback. Core gaming growth nearly 50% YoY.
SNAP: Q3 2026 revenue up mid-teens YoY, broadly in line. Advertising growth slowed to low-to-mid single digits and paid subscribers reached about 30 million.

tension_points.bull_case: Most 2027 capacity is already under construction or permitted, Texas moratoria would be constrained by the legislature, many local bans hit areas with little activity. Broad shutdown is unlikely and GIR expects datacentre focus to fade after the midterms.
tension_points.bear_case: Gerstner argues regulatory friction could stop 10-15 GW of expected 2027 capacity, and SemiAnalysis says 16.7GW of planned 2028 Texas capacity is at risk, on top of Street forecasts well above 30GW.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A broad slowdown in permitting or temporary moratoria that delay 2027 capacity, or chip deliveries outpacing power and site availability.

tension_points.bull_case: There may not be a demand issue for AI chips.
tension_points.bear_case: If power and sites lag chip deliveries, semis could see an inventory correction similar to 2022-23, as AWS stages about $3bn of GB300 racks per month in warehouses.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that delivered chips are being installed and powered on schedule, not staged in warehouses.
